topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's place in the series and introduces its intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Molecular changes driving cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered molecular states give cells cancer-promoting properties, extending mutation-driven clonal selection to epigenetic disruption.

topics.label: Stemness and the cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy influences its capacity to initiate and propagate a tumor.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness and cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stemness on mutation-bearing cells and enable tumor development.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive surrounding cells as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for studying cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tissue-based molecular analysis can reveal tumor evolution and interactions within the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Converging conditions for malignant evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains how cancer depends on favorable conditions coinciding and extends that argument to developmental susceptibility in childhood cancers.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and identifies cancer therapy as the next lecture's subject.
